record.narrative:
The twelve new comparisons are mostly confirmatory robustness tests rather than new main predictors. TP53 loss versus no TP53 loss remains a very large weaker-dependency association in the Avana stratum (+0.830; R27) and in the smaller non-Avana stratum (+0.813; R28); KEAP1 loss versus no KEAP1 loss remains a very large weaker-dependency association in the Avana stratum (+0.801; R29); SMARCA4 loss versus no SMARCA4 loss remains a very large stronger-dependency association in the Avana stratum (+0.787; R30, signed to the accepted negative direction). I accept H39, H40, H17, and H20 because their signed point estimates and entire 95% intervals are far above the 0.15-unit threshold. The non-Avana TP53 stratum has modest cell sizes, so I keep it active but do not treat it as stronger than the Avana result.

Single-wildtype genetic contexts also remain threshold-level: TP53 loss among KEAP1-wildtype cells (+0.800; R34), KEAP1 loss among TP53-wildtype cells (+0.780; R35), and SMARCA4 loss among TP53-wildtype cells (+0.833; R36). These are overlapping analyses within the same supplied dataset, not independent replication, but they further reduce the concern that each accepted predictor association is produced mainly by co-occurrence with the other two accepted predictor losses. I accept H14, H15, and H18.

Adenocarcinoma interactions for TP53 and KEAP1 do not support threshold-level subgroup modification: TP53 interaction is signed -0.005 with upper bound +0.130 (R31), and KEAP1 interaction is signed -0.035 with upper bound +0.102 (R32). Because both claimed-direction upper bounds are below 0.15, I reject and close H41 and H42. The Avana-library main effect is similarly not threshold-level (+0.053; R37, upper +0.141), so I reject H38 as evidence of a meaningful overall library difference in the claimed direction.

The SMARCA4-by-adenocarcinoma interaction is different: H24 is signed negative (-0.174; R33, interval -0.312 to -0.035). This does not support the originally claimed direction, so I reject and close H24. However, the same result indicates an uncertain opposite-direction signal: SMARCA4 loss may have a weaker stronger-dependency association in adenocarcinoma than in its complement. When reversed, the interval would span roughly +0.035 to +0.312, with a point estimate above threshold but a lower bound below threshold, so I do not treat the opposite effect as established. I register a new unresolved reversed-direction proposal linked to H24 for possible follow-up.

The strict CDKN2A test remains borderline. In cells wildtype for TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MTAP, CDKN2A loss has a signed estimate of +0.131 (R38; interval +0.065 to +0.196). The point estimate is below the 0.15-unit threshold, although the interval includes threshold-level values. Therefore H49 remains unresolved, and I defer further CDKN2A work unless another strategy can resolve this borderline range. Since SMARCA4 loss is now the strongest accepted main effect without independent validation, I request validation for H4.

prompt:
Iteration 3/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.

record.narrative:
The new validation evidence is decisive for the SMARCA4 main association and satisfies the KEAP1 response deadline. For H4, the independent validation of SMARCA4 loss versus no loss gives a signed estimate of +0.827 with interval +0.731 to +0.924 at the validation alpha level. Because the claim direction is -1, this corresponds to a raw contrast of about -0.827 units: SMARCA4-loss cells are more negative on dependency_composite, i.e. they have stronger composite dependency. The point estimate and the entire interval are far above the 0.15-unit threshold, so I accept H4 and keep it active because the subtype-specific SMARCA4 issue remains unresolved. For H30, the validation split for SMARCA4 loss within TP53- and KEAP1-wildtype cells gives a signed estimate of +0.780 with interval +0.718 to +0.842, also far above threshold. This independently confirms that the SMARCA4 association is not confined to co-mutation context. I accept H30 and close that specific stratum because the claim has now been independently validated and does not require further follow-up. For H3, the due validation gives a signed estimate of +0.738 with interval +0.644 to +0.831 for KEAP1 loss. This is consistent with discovery R3 and confirms a large weaker-dependency association. I accept H3 and keep it active for remaining subtype/context analyses.

Taken together, the evidence now supports three large dataset associations: TP53 loss with weaker composite dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker composite dependency, and SMARCA4 loss with stronger composite dependency. Each main effect has independent validation in the supplied split, and the KEAP1 and TP53 effects are also robust in combined- and single-wildtype co-mutation strata. These are associations in the supplied screens, not causal statements and not yet evidence of generalizability outside this dataset.

Important negative or unresolved findings remain. Adenocarcinoma-versus-complement interactions for TP53 and KEAP1 do not support threshold-level modification. The SMARCA4-by-adenocarcinoma interaction is the main remaining subgroup uncertainty: the reversed claim H51 has a point estimate above threshold, +0.174, but its lower bound is below threshold, +0.035. Therefore it remains unresolved rather than accepted. Direct adenocarcinoma main effects for the accepted predictors, especially H45 for SMARCA4, are the most informative next discovery analyses. CDKN2A remains borderline: several estimates, including the strict TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4/MTAP-wildtype context, are around +0.13 to +0.14, below the 0.15-unit threshold, though intervals include threshold-level values. I defer CDKN2A work unless validation or a better refinement can resolve the borderline range. STK11 remains unaccepted overall, and its remaining context tests are lower priority, so I defer H47 and H48.

The newly registered analyses are designed to resolve the most informative residual uncertainties. Tests of TP53 within KEAP1-loss cells, KEAP1 within SMARCA4-loss cells, and SMARCA4 within TP53-loss cells will complete the main co-mutation strata for the accepted predictors. TP53 and SMARCA4 tests within adherent culture, complementing KEAP1 adherent test H50, will provide additional technical robustness. Finally, I register three broad exploratory screens for EGFR amplification, PTEN loss, and RB1 loss to avoid overconcentration on the accepted predictors while keeping new comparisons pre-registered and thresholded.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

record.narrative:
The three largest dataset associations are now accepted and independently validated: TP53 loss with weaker composite dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker composite dependency, and SMARCA4 loss with stronger composite dependency. The main unresolved question among the accepted predictors is whether the SMARCA4 association is genuinely attenuated in adenocarcinoma relative to its complement. The original full-population reversed interaction H51/R33 has a point estimate above the 0.15-unit threshold but a lower confidence bound below threshold, so I register a cleaner-background refinement: the SMARCA4-by-adenocarcinoma interaction among TP53- and KEAP1-wildtype cells. A positive signed estimate for this direction-1 claim would mean the raw adenocarcinoma SMARCA4-loss contrast is higher, i.e. less negative, than the complement contrast; biologically that would support adenocarcinoma-specific attenuation of the stronger-dependency association. A null or sub-threshold result would make the earlier attenuation more consistent with co-mutation context, sampling, or unmeasured background confounding rather than a broad subtype effect.

I also register a direct main-effect complement to that interaction: SMARCA4 loss versus no SMARCA4 loss among TP53- and KEAP1-wildtype adenocarcinoma cells. This asks whether the accepted SMARCA4 stronger-dependency association remains threshold-level within adenocarcinoma after removing two common co-occurring predictor losses. The expected raw contrast is negative because SMARCA4-loss cells should be more negative on dependency_composite; because the claim direction is -1, that would appear as a positive signed estimate. Plausible alternatives are that the effect remains large but noisier in the restricted subtype, that it falls below threshold if adenocarcinoma attenuation is real, or that the restriction creates unstable estimates.

For CDKN2A, the existing estimates are consistently below the 0.15-unit threshold but often have intervals that include threshold-level effects. I register a strict genetic background refinement: CDKN2A loss among cells wildtype for TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MTAP, restricted to adenocarcinoma. If a threshold-level stronger-dependency effect is concentrated in adenocarcinoma, this analysis may support further validation; if it remains below threshold, it strengthens the case that CDKN2A is not a scientifically meaningful driver in this dataset under the pre-specified effect-size criterion.

Finally, I register four broad exploratory predictor screens: MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, BRAF V600E, and ERBB2 amplification. These are intended to test whether any other measured oncogenic alteration is associated with a threshold-level dependency-composite difference rather than concentrating all discovery on the three already accepted predictors. MYC amplification is the only screen with a specific stronger-dependency expectation, because MYC-amplified cells may have greater transcriptional or replication stress; the others are registered in the stronger-dependency direction as plausible but uncertain oncogenic-driver hypotheses, with null threshold-level differences as equally plausible alternatives. All new proposals are pre-registered associations to be judged against the 0.15-unit threshold; none is initially treated as causal or generalizable outside the supplied dataset.

The first three analyses target the principal remaining accepted-predictor uncertainty: whether SMARCA4 loss has an attenuated stronger-dependency association in adenocarcinoma. H45 estimates the direct SMARCA4 main effect within all adenocarcinoma cells; H61 estimates the same main effect within TP53- and KEAP1-wildtype adenocarcinoma cells; and H60 estimates the adenocarcinoma-versus-complement interaction in the same clean TP53/KEAP1-wildtype background. Because estimates are signed to the registered directions, H60 positive signed values support attenuation (a smaller stronger-dependency association in adenocarcinoma than in the complement), while null or sub-threshold values would make the earlier reversed full-population interaction more consistent with sampling or co-mutation background. The next three analyses, H52 through H54, test whether each accepted predictor association remains threshold-level inside cells carrying one of the other accepted predictor losses. These are not independent replication analyses, but they assess whether the large associations are robust to pairwise co-occurring genetic context rather than being confined to wildtype backgrounds. The remaining six analyses are broad, pre-registered predictor screens for EGFR amplification, PTEN loss, RB1 loss, MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, and ERBB2 amplification. These prevent the run from becoming solely a confirmation exercise around the three accepted predictors and test whether any other common measured alteration is associated with a threshold-level dependency-composite difference. I defer additional CDKN2A and culture-stratified analyses for now because multiple CDKN2A estimates are below the 0.15-unit threshold and are likely poorly resolved by further subgroup restrictions, whereas the requested set combines the most focused unresolved accepted-predictor question with broad discovery coverage.

prompt:
Iteration 4/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

CDKN2A remains deferred/borderline; culture robustness and STK11 contexts are lower priority pending these results.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The three largest dataset associations are now accepted and independently validated: TP53 loss with weaker composite dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker composite dependency, and SMARCA4 loss with stronger composite dependency. The original full-population reversed interaction H51/R33 has a point estimate above the 0.15-unit threshold but a lower confidence bound below threshold, so I register a cleaner-background refinement: the SMARCA4-by-adenocarcinoma interaction among TP53- and KEAP1-wildtype cells. A positive signed estimate for this direction-1 claim would mean the raw adenocarcinoma SMARCA4-loss contrast is higher, i.e. less negative, than the complement contrast; biologically that would support adenocarcinoma-specific attenuation of the stronger-dependency association. A null or sub-threshold result would make the earlier attenuation more consistent with co-mutation context, sampling, or unmeasured background confounding rather than a broad subtype effect.\n\nI also register a direct main-effect complement to that interaction: SMARCA4 loss versus no SMARCA4 loss among TP53- and KEAP1-wildtype adenocarcinoma cells. The expected raw contrast is negative because SMARCA4-loss cells should be more negative on dependency_composite; because the claim direction is -1, that would appear as a positive signed estimate. Plausible alternatives are that the effect remains large but noisier in the restricted subtype, that it falls below threshold if adenocarcinoma attenuation is real, or that the restriction creates unstable estimates.\n\nFor CDKN2A, the existing estimates are consistently below the 0.15-unit threshold but often have intervals that include threshold-level effects. If a threshold-level stronger-dependency effect is concentrated in adenocarcinoma, this analysis may support further validation; if it remains below threshold, it strengthens the case that CDKN2A is not a scientifically meaningful driver in this dataset under the pre-specified effect-size criterion.\n\nFinally, I register four broad exploratory predictor screens: MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, BRAF V600E, and ERBB2 amplification. These are intended to test whether any other measured oncogenic alteration is associated with a threshold-level dependency-composite difference rather than concentrating all discovery on the three already accepted predictors. MYC amplification is the only screen with a specific stronger-dependency expectation, because MYC-amplified cells may have greater transcriptional or replication stress; the others are registered in the stronger-dependency direction as plausible but uncertain oncogenic-driver hypotheses, with null threshold-level differences as equally plausible alternatives. H45 estimates the direct SMARCA4 main effect within all adenocarcinoma cells; H61 estimates the same main effect within TP53- and KEAP1-wildtype adenocarcinoma cells; and H60 estimates the adenocarcinoma-versus-complement interaction in the same clean TP53/KEAP1-wildtype background. Because estimates are signed to the registered directions, H60 positive signed values support attenuation (a smaller stronger-dependency association in adenocarcinoma than in the complement), while null or sub-threshold values would make the earlier reversed full-population interaction more consistent with sampling or co-mutation background. The next three analyses, H52 through H54, test whether each accepted predictor association remains threshold-level inside cells carrying one of the other accepted predictor losses. These are not independent replication analyses, but they assess whether the large associations are robust to pairwise co-occurring genetic context rather than being confined to wildtype backgrounds. record.narrative:
I assessed the twelve new discovery results against the pre-specified 0.15-unit threshold, using estimates as signed to each registered direction. The clean-background SMARCA4-by-adenocarcinoma interaction H60/R41 is not threshold-level: signed estimate +0.065 with interval -0.040 to +0.170. The upper bound barely exceeds threshold while the lower bound remains near zero, so this exact refinement does not support established adenocarcinoma-specific attenuation. I close H60 as unresolved. Direct SMARCA4 main effects remain very large in adenocarcinoma: H45/R43 gives +0.760 (0.686 to 0.833), and the cleaner TP53/KEAP1-wildtype adenocarcinoma stratum H61/R42 gives +0.796 (0.743 to 0.848), both with entire intervals far above threshold. These accept H45 and H61 as dataset associations and close those specific subtype main-effect tests. The co-occurring genetic contexts also remain robust and threshold-level: TP53 loss within KEAP1-loss cells H52/R44 +0.878 (0.773 to 0.982), KEAP1 loss within SMARCA4-loss cells H53/R45 +0.790 (0.661 to 0.920), and SMARCA4 loss within TP53-loss cells H54/R46 +0.763 (0.653 to 0.873). I accept and close H52, H53, and H54 as context-robustness checks; they reduce concern that the accepted main associations disappear in one another's presence, but they are not independent replication.

The most consequential new result is PTEN loss H58/R48. In the claimed stronger-dependency direction, the signed estimate is +0.239 with interval +0.145 to +0.332. Both the point estimate and entire interval exceed 0.15, so I accept H58 in the supplied discovery data. Because PTEN was not among the originally accepted predictors and because its measured co-occurrence with TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 losses could plausibly explain part of the association, I request independent validation for H58 and keep it active. I also register a clean-background PTEN refinement among TP53-, KEAP1-, and SMARCA4-wildtype cells to test whether the PTEN association is independent of the three dominant accepted associations.

The remaining broad screens do not support meaningful claimed-direction threshold effects. EGFR amplification H57/R47 is borderline in an ambiguous way: signed estimate +0.102 with interval -0.003 to +0.206. The point estimate is below threshold and the interval includes both no effect and threshold-level benefit, so I leave H57 unresolved but defer it rather than allocate additional validation before PTEN is resolved. RB1 loss H59/R49, MYC amplification H63/R50, PIK3CA mutation H64/R51, and ERBB2 amplification H66/R52 all have claimed-direction intervals below threshold, including upper bounds under 0.15, and I reject and close them as not supporting the registered hypotheses. Given the new PTEN signal and the clean-background SMARCA4 interaction result, I defer the remaining full-population SMARCA4-by-adenocarcinoma reversed interaction H51; it remains unresolved, but it is lower priority than establishing whether PTEN is a robust measured predictor and whether it is independent of accepted co-mutation structure. All accepted findings remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal effects or validated generalizable biomarkers.

prompt:
Iteration 4/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
Final synthesis for iteration 4: the response deadline for H13 is satisfied by independent validation. For the accepted TP53 main association, the validation estimate is +0.795 with interval +0.709 to +0.881 at the validation alpha level, using the registered direction +1. Because this is a positive raw contrast, TP53-loss cells have less negative dependency_composite scores, i.e. weaker composite dependency. The effect is far above the 0.15-unit threshold and is also strongly supported in discovery (+0.829, interval +0.767 to +0.891). I therefore keep H13 accepted. The related TP53 subtype, culture, and co-mutation tests remain active as separate context questions, but the overall TP53 main effect itself is now independently validated in the supplied split.

The new PTEN validation materially changes the interpretation of H58. The original PTEN estimate was +0.239 in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, with interval +0.145 to +0.332. That interval is not entirely above the 0.15-unit threshold because the lower bound is slightly below threshold, although the point estimate is above it. The independent validation gives +0.195 with interval +0.062 to +0.328. The validation point estimate remains positive and above threshold, but the interval is much wider and its lower bound is far below the scientifically meaningful threshold. Combining these results, PTEN loss is a borderline positive signal for stronger composite dependency in this supplied dataset, but the evidence does not establish a threshold-level association with the precision that would justify an accepted claim. I therefore change H58 from accepted to unresolved and keep it active. The clean-background test H67, PTEN loss among TP53-, KEAP1-, and SMARCA4-wildtype cells, is the most informative next PTEN analysis because it can distinguish an independent PTEN association from confounding by the three dominant accepted predictors.

The currently supported dataset-level findings are large and well replicated in the supplied split: TP53 loss is associated with weaker composite dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker composite dependency; and SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger composite dependency. These are not single-gene knockout measurements; dependency_composite is a composite score, and the conclusions are associations within this dataset, not causal statements or generalized biomarker claims. The robustness analyses strengthen the three main findings without making them causal: TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 effects remain threshold-level within Avana and non-Avana library strata and within relevant single- and double-wildtype co-mutation contexts. SMARCA4 also remains threshold-level in adenocarcinoma overall and within TP53/KEAP1-wildtype adenocarcinoma cells. The adenocarcinoma-subtype modification question is not settled: full-population SMARCA4-by-adenocarcinoma attenuation remains unresolved, while the cleaner TP53/KEAP1-wildtype interaction estimate was +0.065 with interval -0.040 to +0.170, which does not establish attenuation.

Important unresolved or negative findings include PTEN and CDKN2A. PTEN, now downgraded to unresolved, should not be interpreted as an accepted threshold-level predictor. CDKN2A estimates cluster around +0.13 to +0.14 in stricter genetic backgrounds and in adenocarcinoma, below or straddling the 0.15-unit threshold, so CDKN2A remains a borderline unresolved signal rather than an accepted predictor. Several broad exploratory comparisons are negative or unsupported in their claimed directions: research markers D/E/F, KRAS mutation, ERBB2 amplification, MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, RB1 loss, and the overall Avana-library main effect. TP53 and KEAP1 adenocarcinoma interactions also do not support threshold-level subgroup modification. EGFR amplification is borderline and deferred rather than accepted.

The best next analysis is H67: estimate PTEN loss in the clean TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-wildtype background. If H67 produces a threshold-level positive signed interval, it would justify a further PTEN validation decision and would support PTEN as a potentially independent measured predictor. If H67 is null or remains borderline, PTEN should likely be classified as an unsupported borderline signal in this dataset. More generally, further work should prioritize focused robustness and independence questions for accepted predictors over additional broad subgroup hunting, and should continue to separate supplied-dataset associations from causality and external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 5/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

Future plan: focused follow-up for PTEN independence, then culture/technical robustness for accepted predictors and remaining subtype questions only if informative.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The three largest dataset associations are now accepted and independently validated: TP53 loss with weaker composite dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker composite dependency, and SMARCA4 loss with stronger composite dependency. The main unresolved question among the accepted predictors is whether the SMARCA4 association is genuinely attenuated in adenocarcinoma relative to its complement. The original full-population reversed interaction H51/R33 has a point estimate above the 0.15-unit threshold but a lower confidence bound below threshold, so I register a cleaner-background refinement: the SMARCA4-by-adenocarcinoma interaction among TP53- and KEAP1-wildtype cells. A positive signed estimate for this direction-1 claim would mean the raw adenocarcinoma SMARCA4-loss contrast is higher, i.e. less negative, than the complement contrast; biologically that would support adenocarcinoma-specific attenuation of the stronger-dependency association. A null or sub-threshold result would make the earlier attenuation more consistent with co-mutation context, sampling, or unmeasured background confounding rather than a broad subtype effect.\n\nI also register a direct main-effect complement to that interaction: SMARCA4 loss versus no SMARCA4 loss among TP53- and KEAP1-wildtype adenocarcinoma cells. This asks whether the accepted SMARCA4 stronger-dependency association remains threshold-level within adenocarcinoma after removing two common co-occurring predictor losses. The expected raw contrast is negative because SMARCA4-loss cells should be more negative on dependency_composite; because the claim direction is -1, that would appear as a positive signed estimate. Plausible alternatives are that the effect remains large but noisier in the restricted subtype, that it falls below threshold if adenocarcinoma attenuation is real, or that the restriction creates unstable estimates.\n\nFor CDKN2A, the existing estimates are consistently below the 0.15-unit threshold but often have intervals that include threshold-level effects. I register a strict genetic background refinement: CDKN2A loss among cells wildtype for TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MTAP, restricted to adenocarcinoma. If a threshold-level stronger-dependency effect is concentrated in adenocarcinoma, this analysis may support further validation; if it remains below threshold, it strengthens the case that CDKN2A is not a scientifically meaningful driver in this dataset under the pre-specified effect-size criterion.\n\nFinally, I register four broad exploratory predictor screens: MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, BRAF V600E, and ERBB2 amplification. These are intended to test whether any other measured oncogenic alteration is associated with a threshold-level dependency-composite difference rather than concentrating all discovery on the three already accepted predictors. MYC amplification is the only screen with a specific stronger-dependency expectation, because MYC-amplified cells may have greater transcriptional or replication stress; the others are registered in the stronger-dependency direction as plausible but uncertain oncogenic-driver hypotheses, with null threshold-level differences as equally plausible alternatives. All new proposals are pre-registered associations to be judged against the 0.15-unit threshold; none is initially treated as causal or generalizable outside the supplied dataset.","analyze":"I request 12 unrun discovery analyses and make no new assessments at this analyze stage. H45 estimates the direct SMARCA4 main effect within all adenocarcinoma cells; H61 estimates the same main effect within TP53- and KEAP1-wildtype adenocarcinoma cells; and H60 estimates the adenocarcinoma-versus-complement interaction in the same clean TP53/KEAP1-wildtype background. Because estimates are signed to the registered directions, H60 positive signed values support attenuation (a smaller stronger-dependency association in adenocarcinoma than in the complement), while null or sub-threshold values would make the earlier reversed full-population interaction more consistent with sampling or co-mutation background. The next three analyses, H52 through H54, test whether each accepted predictor association remains threshold-level inside cells carrying one of the other accepted predictor losses. These are not independent replication analyses, but they assess whether the large associations are robust to pairwise co-occurring genetic context rather than being confined to wildtype backgrounds. The remaining six analyses are broad, pre-registered predictor screens for EGFR amplification, PTEN loss, RB1 loss, MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, and ERBB2 amplification. These prevent the run from becoming solely a confirmation exercise around the three accepted predictors and test whether any other common measured alteration is associated with a threshold-level dependency-composite difference. The upper bound barely exceeds threshold while the lower bound remains near zero, so this exact refinement does not support established adenocarcinoma-specific attenuation. I close H60 as unresolved. Direct SMARCA4 main effects remain very large in adenocarcinoma: H45/R43 gives +0.760 (0.686 to 0.833), and the cleaner TP53/KEAP1-wildtype adenocarcinoma stratum H61/R42 gives +0.796 (0.743 to 0.848), both with entire intervals far above threshold. These accept H45 and H61 as dataset associations and close those specific subtype main-effect tests. The co-occurring genetic contexts also remain robust and threshold-level: TP53 loss within KEAP1-loss cells H52/R44 +0.878 (0.773 to 0.982), KEAP1 loss within SMARCA4-loss cells H53/R45 +0.790 (0.661 to 0.920), and SMARCA4 loss within TP53-loss cells H54/R46 +0.763 (0.653 to 0.873). I accept and close H52, H53, and H54 as context-robustness checks; they reduce concern that the accepted main associations disappear in one another's presence, but they are not independent replication.\n\nThe most consequential new result is PTEN loss H58/R48. In the claimed stronger-dependency direction, the signed estimate is +0.239 with interval +0.145 to +0.332. record.narrative:
No assessments are due, so this stage registers new comparisons only. The current top dataset associations are TP53 loss with weaker composite dependency under H13, KEAP1 loss with weaker composite dependency under H3, and SMARCA4 loss with stronger composite dependency under H4. The highest-value unresolved follow-up remains PTEN and CDKN2A, both borderline in the claimed stronger-dependency direction. For PTEN, I register a stricter genetic-background refinement among TP53-, KEAP1-, SMARCA4-, and MTAP-wildtype cells, plus a TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-wildtype adenocarcinoma-specific main effect. These extend H67 without adding many more PTEN tests: a threshold-level clean-background result would justify reconsidering PTEN as a genuine predictor, while a subthreshold or null result would argue against treating PTEN as scientifically meaningful in this dataset.

For CDKN2A, prior estimates cluster below but near the 0.15-unit threshold. I register CDKN2A loss within MTAP-loss cells and a CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction to test whether the CDKN2A signal is concentrated in a specific deletion/loss context or diluted in isolated deletions. If either result is threshold-level in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, CDKN2A becomes worth additional resolution; otherwise the accumulated evidence supports treating it as borderline or not meaningfully associated under the pre-specified threshold.

The accepted predictors now need technical and biological robustness checks beyond library and co-mutation context. I register interactions with high versus lower Cas9 activity for TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4. Because the estimates are signed to the registered directions, positive signed estimates for TP53 and KEAP1 mean the raw positive/weaker-dependency contrast is larger in the higher-activity group than in the complement, while a positive signed estimate for the direction -1 SMARCA4 claim means the raw negative/stronger-dependency contrast is more negative in the higher-activity group. Such results would suggest the associations are not merely attenuated or distorted by low-Cas9 assay conditions; null or reversed interactions would not invalidate the main associations but would indicate context dependence.

I also register SMARCA4 interactions with fast growth and high ploidy. SMARCA4 is the accepted predictor with an opposite dependency direction, and composite dependency could be influenced by proliferation or chromosomal instability context. These tests ask whether the strong SMARCA4 association remains similar, weaker, or stronger in more proliferative or aneuploid backgrounds, and whether it survives basic biological context rather than only technical/co-mutation robustness.

Finally, I include broad screens for APC mutation, SMAD4 loss, and NF1 loss, all initially claimed in the stronger-dependency direction but with uncertain anticipated raw contrast. These variables have sufficient sample size and complement the previously screened KRAS, MYC, PIK3CA, ERBB2, EGFR, and RB1 comparisons. All new comparisons remain pre-registered associations in the supplied dataset, with external generalizability and causality explicitly out of scope.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

The original PTEN estimate was +0.239 in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, with interval +0.145 to +0.332. The independent validation gives +0.195 with interval +0.062 to +0.328. The validation point estimate remains positive and above threshold, but the interval is much wider and its lower bound is far below the scientifically meaningful threshold. Combining these results, PTEN loss is a borderline positive signal for stronger composite dependency in this supplied dataset, but the evidence does not establish a threshold-level association with the precision that would justify an accepted claim. I therefore change H58 from accepted to unresolved and keep it active. These are not single-gene knockout measurements; dependency_composite is a composite score, and the conclusions are associations within this dataset, not causal statements or generalized biomarker claims. The robustness analyses strengthen the three main findings without making them causal: TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 effects remain threshold-level within Avana and non-Avana library strata and within relevant single- and double-wildtype co-mutation contexts. record.narrative:
No assessments are due, so this stage requests 12 unrun discovery analyses and makes no claim assessments. The highest-priority new analysis is H67, PTEN loss among TP53-, KEAP1-, and SMARCA4-wildtype cells. This is the decisive independence test for PTEN: a threshold-level positive signed estimate would support PTEN loss as a genuine measured predictor rather than a proxy for the three dominant associations, while a null or sub-threshold result would strongly argue against accepting PTEN despite its borderline overall and validated estimates. I do not request H68 or H69 yet because H67 should determine whether further PTEN subgroup or stricter-background tests are worth the multiplicity cost.

Next, I request Cas9-activity robustness interactions for the three accepted predictors: H72 for TP53, H73 for KEAP1, and H74 for SMARCA4. These test whether the large accepted associations are preserved when comparing higher-Cas9 versus lower-Cas9 assay conditions. Large signed interactions would indicate context dependence on editing efficiency or assay quality; near-null interactions would strengthen the interpretation that the main TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 associations are not simply artifacts of heterogeneous Cas9 performance. These are not validation replications, but they address a key technical-robustness question for all three accepted findings.

I also request main effects within the largest culture context, adherent: H55 for TP53, H50 for KEAP1, and H56 for SMARCA4. These test whether the accepted associations remain threshold-level in the dominant culture setting rather than depending on rare non-adherent contexts. Additionally, H43 and H44 request TP53 and KEAP1 main effects within adenocarcinoma. The adenocarcinoma-by-TP53 and adenocarcinoma-by-KEAP1 interactions were previously rejected, but the direct subtype main effects have not yet been estimated. Estimating them completes the subtype main-effect picture for the accepted predictors, especially since SMARCA4 adenocarcinoma main effects are already established.

For CDKN2A, the accumulated estimates are clustered around but below the 0.15-unit threshold. H70 tests the mechanistically informative context of CDKN2A loss within MTAP-loss cells. This asks whether the borderline CDKN2A signal becomes threshold-level when CDKN2A deletion/loss co-occurs with adjacent MTAP loss, rather than being diluted across isolated deletions. A threshold-level result would justify a focused CDKN2A interaction or validation decision; a sub-threshold result would add support to deprioritizing CDKN2A as a meaningful predictor under the pre-specified threshold.

Finally, H77 and H78 provide broad discovery coverage by testing APC mutation and SMAD4 loss in the claimed stronger-dependency direction. These variables have adequate prevalence and complement previously screened KRAS, MYC, PIK3CA, ERBB2, EGFR, and RB1 comparisons. They reduce the risk that the run becomes overly confirmation-focused. All selected analyses are scored against the 0.15-unit threshold using the registered signed directions, and none should be interpreted as causal or externally generalizable unless further evidence supports such claims.

Iteration 5/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

Priority order: (1) H67 PTEN clean-background test is decisive for PTEN independence from TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4. If H67 is threshold-level and precision sufficient, reconsider PTEN; if borderline/null, deprioritize PTEN and avoid immediate H68/H69. (2) H72-H74 Cas9-activity interactions test technical robustness of accepted TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 associations. (3) H55/H50/H56 adherent-culture main effects test culture robustness; H43/H44 TP53/KEAP1 adenocarcinoma main effects complete subtype main-effect evidence after prior adenocarcinoma interactions. (4) H70 CDKN2A within MTAP-loss tests whether CDKN2A borderline signal is context-specific; if subthreshold, deprioritize CDKN2A. (5) H77 APC and H78 SMAD4 broad screens maintain discovery diversity. Held for possible follow-up: H68/H69 PTEN refinements, H71 CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction, H75/H76 SMARCA4 growth/ploidy interactions, H62 clean-background CDKN2A adenocarcinoma, and remaining co-mutation contexts.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due, so this stage registers new comparisons only. The current top dataset associations are TP53 loss with weaker composite dependency under H13, KEAP1 loss with weaker composite dependency under H3, and SMARCA4 loss with stronger composite dependency under H4. The highest-value unresolved follow-up remains PTEN and CDKN2A, both borderline in the claimed stronger-dependency direction. For PTEN, I register a stricter genetic-background refinement among TP53-, KEAP1-, SMARCA4-, and MTAP-wildtype cells, plus a TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-wildtype adenocarcinoma-specific main effect. These extend H67 without adding many more PTEN tests: a threshold-level clean-background result would justify reconsidering PTEN as a genuine predictor, while a subthreshold or null result would argue against treating PTEN as scientifically meaningful in this dataset.\n\nFor CDKN2A, prior estimates cluster below but near the 0.15-unit threshold. I register CDKN2A loss within MTAP-loss cells and a CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction to test whether the CDKN2A signal is concentrated in a specific deletion/loss context or diluted in isolated deletions. If either result is threshold-level in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, CDKN2A becomes worth additional resolution; otherwise the accumulated evidence supports treating it as borderline or not meaningfully associated under the pre-specified threshold.\n\nThe accepted predictors now need technical and biological robustness checks beyond library and co-mutation context. I register interactions with high versus lower Cas9 activity for TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4. Because the estimates are signed to the registered directions, positive signed estimates for TP53 and KEAP1 mean the raw positive/weaker-dependency contrast is larger in the higher-activity group than in the complement, while a positive signed estimate for the direction -1 SMARCA4 claim means the raw negative/stronger-dependency contrast is more negative in the higher-activity group. Such results would suggest the associations are not merely attenuated or distorted by low-Cas9 assay conditions; null or reversed interactions would not invalidate the main associations but would indicate context dependence.\n\nI also register SMARCA4 interactions with fast growth and high ploidy. SMARCA4 is the accepted predictor with an opposite dependency direction, and composite dependency could be influenced by proliferation or chromosomal instability context. These tests ask whether the strong SMARCA4 association remains similar, weaker, or stronger in more proliferative or aneuploid backgrounds, and whether it survives basic biological context rather than only technical/co-mutation robustness.\n\nFinally, I include broad screens for APC mutation, SMAD4 loss, and NF1 loss, all initially claimed in the stronger-dependency direction but with uncertain anticipated raw contrast. These variables have sufficient sample size and complement the previously screened KRAS, MYC, PIK3CA, ERBB2, EGFR, and RB1 comparisons. All new comparisons remain pre-registered associations in the supplied dataset, with external generalizability and causality explicitly out of scope.","analyze":"No assessments are due, so this stage requests 12 unrun discovery analyses and makes no claim assessments. The highest-priority new analysis is H67, PTEN loss among TP53-, KEAP1-, and SMARCA4-wildtype cells. This is the decisive independence test for PTEN: a threshold-level positive signed estimate would support PTEN loss as a genuine measured predictor rather than a proxy for the three dominant associations, while a null or sub-threshold result would strongly argue against accepting PTEN despite its borderline overall and validated estimates. I do not request H68 or H69 yet because H67 should determine whether further PTEN subgroup or stricter-background tests are worth the multiplicity cost.\n\nNext, I request Cas9-activity robustness interactions for the three accepted predictors: H72 for TP53, H73 for KEAP1, and H74 for SMARCA4. These test whether the large accepted associations are preserved when comparing higher-Cas9 versus lower-Cas9 assay conditions. Large signed interactions would indicate context dependence on editing efficiency or assay quality; near-null interactions would strengthen the interpretation that the main TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 associations are not simply artifacts of heterogeneous Cas9 performance. These are not validation replications, but they address a key technical-robustness question for all three accepted findings.\n\nI also request main effects within the largest culture context, adherent: H55 for TP53, H50 for KEAP1, and H56 for SMARCA4. These test whether the accepted associations remain threshold-level in the dominant culture setting rather than depending on rare non-adherent contexts. Additionally, H43 and H44 request TP53 and KEAP1 main effects within adenocarcinoma. The adenocarcinoma-by-TP53 and adenocarcinoma-by-KEAP1 interactions were previously rejected, but the direct subtype main effects have not yet been estimated. Estimating them completes the subtype main-effect picture for the accepted predictors, especially since SMARCA4 adenocarcinoma main effects are already established.\n\nFor CDKN2A, the accumulated estimates are clustered around but below the 0.15-unit threshold. H70 tests the mechanistically informative context of CDKN2A loss within MTAP-loss cells. This asks whether the borderline CDKN2A signal becomes threshold-level when CDKN2A deletion/loss co-occurs with adjacent MTAP loss, rather than being diluted across isolated deletions. A threshold-level result would justify a focused CDKN2A interaction or validation decision; a sub-threshold result would add support to deprioritizing CDKN2A as a meaningful predictor under the pre-specified threshold.\n\nFinally, H77 and H78 provide broad discovery coverage by testing APC mutation and SMAD4 loss in the claimed stronger-dependency direction. These variables have adequate prevalence and complement previously screened KRAS, MYC, PIK3CA, ERBB2, EGFR, and RB1 comparisons. They reduce the risk that the run becomes overly confirmation-focused. All selected analyses are scored against the 0.15-unit threshold using the registered signed directions, and none should be interpreted as causal or externally generalizable unless further evidence supports such claims.","appraise":"I assessed the twelve new discovery results against the pre-specified 0.15-unit threshold, using estimates as signed to each registered direction. The clean-background SMARCA4-by-adenocarcinoma interaction H60/R41 is not threshold-level: signed estimate +0.065 with interval -0.040 to +0.170. The upper bound barely exceeds threshold while the lower bound remains near zero, so this exact refinement does not support established adenocarcinoma-specific attenuation. I close H60 as unresolved. Direct SMARCA4 main effects remain very large in adenocarcinoma: H45/R43 gives +0.760 (0.686 to 0.833), and the cleaner TP53/KEAP1-wildtype adenocarcinoma stratum H61/R42 gives +0.796 (0.743 to 0.848), both with entire intervals far above threshold. These accept H45 and H61 as dataset associations and close those specific subtype main-effect tests. The co-occurring genetic contexts also remain robust and threshold-level: TP53 loss within KEAP1-loss cells H52/R44 +0.878 (0.773 to 0.982), KEAP1 loss within SMARCA4-loss cells H53/R45 +0.790 (0.661 to 0.920), and SMARCA4 loss within TP53-loss cells H54/R46 +0.763 (0.653 to 0.873). I accept and close H52, H53, and H54 as context-robustness checks; they reduce concern that the accepted main associations disappear in one another's presence, but they are not independent replication.\n\nThe most consequential new result is PTEN loss H58/R48. In the claimed stronger-dependency direction, the signed estimate is +0.239 with interval +0.145 to +0.332. Both the point estimate and entire interval exceed 0.15, so I accept H58 in the supplied discovery data. Because PTEN was not among the originally accepted predictors and because its measured co-occurrence with TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 losses could plausibly explain part of the association, I request independent validation for H58 and keep it active. I also register a clean-background PTEN refinement among TP53-, KEAP1-, and SMARCA4-wildtype cells to test whether the PTEN association is independent of the three dominant accepted associations.\n\nThe remaining broad screens do not support meaningful claimed-direction threshold effects.
